title: Flatten Nested
statement: Implement `solve(value)`. `value` is a tree of lists. Lists may contain integers or further lists. Strings are not used. Return one flat list of the integers in left-to-right order. An integer at the top level is a one-element list. An empty list returns an empty list.
constraints: Order is preorder of the leaves
hints: If the value is a list, extend the result with a recursive flatten of each child.
If the value is an int, it is a leaf.
Do not flatten by assuming a fixed depth.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: The type test is the recursion structure: a list is an internal node and an int is a leaf.

editorial: The type test is the recursion structure: a list is an internal node and an int is a leaf. A one-level comprehension stops too early on a nested list. The base case is the integer, not the empty list. The empty list simply contributes no children.
